items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: How was Rama Natha before he met the sage and started working in his fields?
items.answer: Before meeting the Sage and started working in his fields, Rama Natha was a lazy man. He spent most of his time looking for a magic potion. He believed that if he had the magic potion that could convert anything to gold, he would become wealthy.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: How did Rama Natha's wife help him in gaining wealth?
items.answer: Rama Natha's wife helped him in gaining wealth. Rama Natha had planted banana plants on his large tracts of land as suggested by the sage and spent all his time tending to them. This resulted in the banana plants bearing good quality fruit. Rama Natha's wife, Madhumati, gathered the fruit crop and sold it in the market for a good price, and over the years this helped Rama Natha increase his plantation and ultimately, his earnings. This is how Rama Natha's wife helped him in gaining wealth.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: What changes could be noted in Rama Natha's behaviour during the six years when he worked on his banana plantation? What moral do we derive from this story of Rama Natha?
items.answer: Many changes could be noted in Rama Natha's behaviour during the six years when he worked on his banana plantation. During the six years when he worked on his banana plantation, Rama Natha became a very hardworking and responsible man. He took care of his plantation with dedication and stopped chasing a shortcut to get the magic potion that would turn anything into gold. The story of Rama Natha, 'A Bottle of Dew' teaches us the value of hard work through Rama Natha's example. It tells us that there is no shortcut to success or gaining wealth. We must work hard towards our goals consistently to achieve them.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: How was Madhumati different from Rama Natha?
items.answer: Madhumati was different from Rama Natha as she did not believe in the magic potion and was a responsible person. When Rama Natha spent all his time and money looking for the magic potion, she worried that they may lose all their wealth. Also, when Rama Natha was busy collecting dew for the magic potion, she took the crop to the market and sold it for a good price to make profit.

items.answer: Rama Natha was the son of a wealthy landlord and inherited large tracts of land when his father passed away. However, he did not take care of his lands and was determined to find a magic potion that would turn anything into gold so that he

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: If you were Rama Natha's neighbour and he came to ask you about the magic potion, how would you deal with him?
items.answer: If I were Rama Natha's neighbour, I would advise him to stop looking for the magic potion. I would tell him that if such a potion existed, no one would have been poor and someone would have already claimed it. I would ask him to start working and earning money so that he could save his earnings and become rich by working hard. I would also advise him to work on the vast land that his father had left him for farming.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: 'You can plant as many banana plants as you want. But remember, you must look after them yourself and collect the dew with your own hands.' Who is the speaker of these lines? What was his intention behind these words? Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: The speaker of these lines is the wise sage, Mahipati. By asking Rama Natha to plant banana plants and take care of them himself, Mahipati wanted him to learn the importance of hard work and stop chasing after the magic potion. At the end of the story, when Madhumati reveals that she had been selling the banana crop and saving the earnings, Rama Natha understands why the sage had asked him to collect the dew in the first place. He realised that the wise sage wanted him to learn the importance of hard work and dedication. He learned that he had to work hard to become wealthy.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: There is a very famous quote by Booker T. Washington-'Nothing ever comes to one, that is worth having, except as a result of hard work.' Do you think it is true? Justify the statement based on your understanding of the story 'A Bottle of Dew'.
items.answer: Yes, it is true that nothing ever comes to one without putting in effort and working hard. We can easily derive this from the story 'A Bottle of Dew' where Rama Natha spends most of his time and resources looking for a shortcut to create wealth and keeps getting cheated by people. However, taking the wise sage's advice, when Rama Natha works hard to grow and tend to his banana plantation, he eventually becomes rich.

items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: Why did the Raven start to sing?
items.answer: When the fox complimented the Raven and told him that he could be a king if he could sing. Listening to such words of praise from the fox, the Raven forgot that his voice was just a croak and that is why he began to sing.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: What weakness of the Raven's character made him open his mouth to sing and which characteristic of the fox made him successful in his plan?
items.answer: The Raven's weakness of giving in to flattery made him open his mouth to sing. When the fox complimented him, he became foolish with pride and forgot that his voice was melodious or pleasant. He prepared himself to sing and opened his mouth, dropping the food on the ground. On the other hand, the fox was very clever and knew the raven's weakness. Therefore, fox's cleverness made him successful in his plan. By tricking the Raven to open his mouth to sing, the fox got himself the piece of food he wanted from the Raven.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: I'm sure the lesson is worth the price'. What was the lesson and what was the price according to the poem 'The Raven and The Fox'?
items.answer: The lesson was that we must never listen to or believe in is about flattery. The poetry teaches us that flattery is in most cases not true and done for selfish reasons. In the poem, the fox used false compliments to flatter the Raven and succeeded in tricking him. The price paid by the Raven was that he believed in the fox's words and forgot that he was holding a morsel in his beak. As soon as he opened his mouth to sing, he dropped and lost the morsel to the fox.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: The famous English writer and philosopher John Ruskin once said, 'Pride is at the bottom of all great mistakes.' Explain how the poet Jean de La Fontaine uses this idea in her poem with reference to 'The Raven and The Fox'.
items.answer: John Ruskin's statement that pride is at the cause of all great mistakes is reflected in Jean de La Fontaine's poem the Raven and the Fox. Fooled by the fox's false compliments, the Raven becomes full of pride and makes the mistake of forgetting that his voice is just a croak. He prepares to sing and opens his beak, dropping the morsel on the ground. This shows that his judgement was affected by fox's flattery which prevented him from making the right decision. Therefore, this poem serves as a lesson to all of us. We must not let the words of others fill us with pride and forget our true personality.

items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: What was the man's reaction when he realised that there was a thief in the house?
items.answer: When the man realised that there was a thief in the house, he first became alert. However, he remained calm and very cleverly handled the whole situation. He even asked his wife to remain calm and devised ab clever plan to get the attention of the village Kotwal, Rama.

items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: How did the man and his wife fool the thief?
items.answer: The man and his wife started talking about their future child's name loudly to deceive the thief. By calling out the name "Rama" as if they were calling their child, they succeeded in alerting their village Kotwal Rama.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: Do you think the Kotwal was smart? Give one reason for your answer.
items.answer: Yes, I think the Kotwal was very smart. When he heard the man's wife calling his name out loudly, he immediately ran in that direction. He must have realised that there was a problem and he needed to go to the house from which the noise was coming. After reaching the house, he noticed the hole in the wall and understood the situation. He stealthily entered the house and caught the thief without giving him a chance to escape. This shows that the Kotwal was indeed smart.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: In the story, what characteristics do you think the Kotwal and the couple had in common?
items.answer: In the story, 'Rama to the rescue', the couple and the Kotwal were similar. They all shared the characteristics of being smart and clever. Besides being smart, they also were calm when the thief had entered the house and handled the situation very well. The couple quickly devised a plan to alert the Kotwal and the Kotwal responded promptly by catching the thief.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: "Calmness is the cradle of power". Justify this statement based on your understanding of the story 'Rama to the Rescue'.
items.answer: It is true to say that calmness is the cradle of power. When one is calm, one can find solutions to every problem. The story 'Rama to the rescue' presents the truth of the statement. The story could have taken a different turn if the man and his wife had not remained calm in the given situation. The thief could have escaped or attacked them if they had started screaming for help. However, they remained calm and did the right thing by alerting their village Kotwal and got the thief arrested. By doing this, the couple protected themselves and others in their village. Thus, we can say, calmness gives us power in any situation.

items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: Why do you think the author chose the title 'The Unlikely Best-friends' for this story?
items.answer: The author chose the title 'The Unlikely Best Friends' for this story as the friends the dog and the elephant, two very different animals become friends. A dog is very different from an elephant in all aspects. However, in the story we see that they play together, eat together and overcome their differences. Even though it is very 'unlikely' or unexpected, the dog and the elephant still become best-friends.

items.section_heading: VERY SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS
items.stem: Describe the activities Gajaraj and Buntee do together.
items.answer: Gajaraj and the Buntee spend time together, with the Buntee even accompanying Gajaraj for his bath. Gajaraj playfully splashes water on the Buntee and they enjoy each other's company. They eat together and Gajaraj even gives Buntee a ride on his back.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: Describe the first meeting between Gajaraj and Buntee. How did their friendship develop?
items.answer: The first meeting between Gajaraj and Buntee was nothing abnormal. Gajaraj was a royal elephant who lived in the royal stable along. One day, Buntee, a stray dog, wandered into the royal stables. Noticing that the dog was tired and hungry, Gajaraj offered him some of his food, which instantly formed a bond between him and Buntee. Despite their differences, Gajaraj was drawn to Buntee's friendliness. They both began playing together, going to the pond for the bath together, sharing food and spending time in each other's company.This is how their bond grew stronger and they became unlikely bestfriends.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: Explain the role of the farmer in the story. How did his actions contribute to the development of the friendship between Gajaraj and Buntee?
items.answer: The farmer is introduced to us as Buntee, the dog's owner. He initially took Buntee away from Gajaraj as the dog was his pet and he had been looking for the dog for some time. However, when the farmer noticed that Buntee's sadness was due to the absence of his friend, the farmer showed compassion and allowed Buntee to visit Gajaraj. This

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Brief.
items.stem: act of kindness ultimately helped make the friendship between the elephant and the dog stronger. The story teaches us that friendship can blossom between the most unlikely individuals. Give examples from the story to support this statement.
items.answer: The story of Gajaraj and Buntee beautifully shows that friendship can blossom between the most unlikely individuals. Despite their differences in size, species, and needs the elephant and the dog formed a deep bond of friendship. They could not speak, but only show their kindness and happiness to each other. Gajaraj showed his kindness by sharing his food with Buntee. Buntee showed his love for Gajaraj by accompanying him everywhere. They enjoyed each other's company, played together, and cared for each other's well being. This unlikely friendship highlights the power of love and acceptance, showing that true friendship goes beyond outward appearances.

items.section_heading: Answer The Following Questions In Short.
items.stem: Mario, in the story 'The Chair' experiences some challenges as he tries to sit on the invisible chair. Based on your understanding of the story, describe the challenges Mario faces and explain how he overcomes them.
items.answer: Mario faces several challenges while trying to sit on the invisible chair. First, he had to overcome his own disbelief. The concept of an invisible chair seems impossible, and Mario initially struggled to believe if it was real. Second, Mario faced the challenge of actually sitting on something he can't see. This required him to rely on his touch and balance, as well as his trust in his grandfather's words. Finally, Mario had to ignore the reactions of his friends who were making fun of him. At first, they didn't believe him about the invisible chair, which could have been discouraging.
